claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 6 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

Now, to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and other expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for him - I provide everything he needs day-to-day like his food, clothes, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to make sure I have the complete picture:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living in any residential accommodation, or does he live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually... he was in care for a short period recently - just a couple of months. But other than that, he lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand this a bit better as it may affect eligibility.

**Is Alex still in care now, or has he returned home to live with you? And when exactly did this care period happen - can you tell me the dates or how many weeks he was in care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's back home with me now. He was in care for 7 weeks - it was just recently, and then he came back home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's really helpful information.

Just to make sure I have everything I need:

**During those 7 weeks when Alex was in care, did he spend any regular time at home with you - for example, did he come home for at least 24 hours each week, or spend any nights at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he was in care full-time during those 7 weeks. He didn't come home for visits or overnight stays during that period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or have you been the only person claiming for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me - I'm the only one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✅ **Alex meets the age requirement** - He's 6 years old (under 16)

✅ **You live in the UK** and are responsible for Alex's care

✅ **Alex lives with you** and you provide for his day-to-day needs

✅ **The care period doesn't affect your eligibility** - Although Alex was in care for 7 weeks recently, this is within the 8-week period during which Child Benefit normally continues. Since he's now back home with you and no one else claimed during that time, your eligibility is not affected.

✅ **No one else is claiming** for Alex

You meet all the criteria for Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you were already claiming and had concerns about the care period, your entitlement should have continued throughout.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
